analysis: Examined base text of ProviderLoop+ModelLoading.swift lines 1-1046 (weight-hash capture/publish, reusable SSD load finalization, ensureModelLoaded admission, load-gate, post-load hash TOCTOU check). Changed ranges in the file_changes (base 1305-1313 onward, head 1305-1349 etc.) fall past the supplied base text (ends at 1046) and the patch excerpt is truncated, so the actual modification (reclaimableMemoryGb/reclaimableMemoryBytes gaining a countingRetainedKVSegments parameter, new evictionCanReach helper delegating to ModelLoadAdmission.evictionCanReach, and release-for-load changes) is only partially visible. Visible patch portion is memory-accounting/eviction-feasibility logic: it changes how reclaimable memory is estimated for admission (availability/DoS-class, T-029/T-010 neighbourhood) and does not touch weight-hash verification, attestation, encryption, cache keys, or coordinator messaging. Existing security-relevant behavior in the supplied base: fresh cryptographic hash bracketing for reusable SSD cache (T-041 mitigation: weightHash binding, fail-closed on mismatch via finalizeReusableSSDLoad; unavailable hash disables SSD reuse and removes stale hash from registration), GLM artifact checks, and shutdown/cancellation handling. None are shown as modified in visible ranges. Remaining questions for integration: (1) the rest of the patch (head lines 1342-1589, including releaseReclaimableMemoryForLoad and the evictUntilAvailable callers) was not visible; verify that over-crediting retained KV segments cannot cause admission of loads that exceed real memory (OOM/availability) and that the post-release memory sample remains authoritative; (2) confirm no change to the weight-hash/ssd gating lines. No concrete security regression identified from supplied evidence.
